sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Algorithmic Fairness & Impossibility Explorer! Here you can experiment with base prevalence rates and decision thresholds across two sub-populations. Toggle between the policy presets above to observe how satisfying calibration directly impacts the false positive rate gap.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the real-time metrics dashboard above us, Nova! In Preset 1, unconstrained thresholds leave a major demographic disparity. Switch to Preset 2 for demographic parity, Preset 3 for equal opportunity, or Preset 4 to see the calibrated COMPAS dilemma firsthand!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: We have docked at Active Checkpoint 1! Evaluate the automated hiring screening scenario above to determine whether a statutory violation of Title VII has occurred under the EEOC Four-Fifths Rule.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 1 time! Group zero has a selection rate of twenty percent, while Group one has thirty percent. What is the Disparate Impact Ratio, and does it breach the EEOC eighty percent threshold? Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! The Disparate Impact Ratio is zero point twenty divided by zero point thirty, which equals zero point six six seven. Because zero point six six seven is strictly less than zero point eighty, this establishes a prima facie statutory violation under the EEOC Four-Fifths Rule and Title VII!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Careful! Statutory compliance under the EEOC Four-Fifths Rule evaluates the ratio of selection rates, not absolute percentage differences. The Disparate Impact Ratio is zero point twenty divided by zero point thirty, which is zero point six six seven—well below the legal eighty percent barrier!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: We have arrived at the Proxy Leakage & Mutual Information Workbench! Test how auxiliary features leak sensitive protected attributes even when the protected column is completely deleted. Toggle different feature combinations and model capacities above us.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the mutual information meter above us, Nova! In Preset 1, even though race was dropped, the non-linear model reconstructs race with ninety-one percent accuracy using ZIP code and commute radius alone! Switch to Preset 4 to verify orthogonalized sanitization!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Active Checkpoint 2! Diagnose why ProPublica and Northpointe could both be mathematically correct in the famous COMPAS recidivism conflict.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Checkpoint 2! ProPublica proved false positive rates were doubled for Black defendants, while Northpointe proved risk calibration was identical across races. How can both statements be mathematically true at the same time? Choose Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Precisely correct! Because underlying base arrest rates differed between populations due to historical policing patterns, Kleinberg's Impossibility Theorem and Bayes' rule mathematically mandate that holding predictive calibration equal strictly forces unequal false positive rates! Both organizations were citing accurate mathematics under competing fairness definitions.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Not quite! ProPublica made no calculation error, and adding more training data cannot overcome a mathematical theorem. Under Kleinberg's theorem, whenever base prevalence rates differ, equal calibration mathematically dictates disparate false positive rates!
